I am 68 years old this year, and I have been farming my 6 mu of land in Quzhou County since I was a young man. My father farmed this same land before me, and his father before him. I only finished primary school, but I know my fields well—every low spot, every place the water runs, and every year the weather is different.

This year, I will do what I have always done, because it works. I will plant **winter wheat** on all 6 mu in the autumn, and after I harvest it in early June, I will immediately plant **summer maize** on the same 6 mu. This is the double-crop rotation that every farmer around here uses. The wheat grows through the winter and spring, and the maize grows through the summer. You cannot let the land sit idle in summer—the heat and sunlight are too valuable to waste.

For the wheat, I will buy **improved seeds** from the seed station. I have used Jimai 22 and Liangxing 99 before, and they do well here. I will use the **rotary tiller** to prepare the soil before sowing in October. I will put down compound fertilizer as a basal dressing—about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, which gives me roughly 18 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 3 kg of potassium per mu. Then in the spring, when the wheat is greening up and at the jointing stage, I will topdress with urea. I will irrigate **4 times**: once before winter to protect the seedlings from the cold, once at green-up in March, once at jointing, and once at heading if the spring is dry. I will spray pesticide **3 times**—herbicide once after sowing, and insecticide twice in the spring when the aphids come. If I see disease on the leaves, I might spray fungicide too, but usually the 3 sprays are enough. I expect about **450 kg per mu** of wheat if the weather cooperates.

For the maize, I will sow immediately after wheat harvest in June. There is no time to plough—the season is short, and the soil is still moist from the wheat irrigation. I will use **no-tillage** direct seeding with a **hybrid** variety like Denghai 605, which is what the seed dealer always has. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing, roughly 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu, and then topdress with urea at the big喇叭口 stage. I will irrigate **2 times**: once at jointing and once at filling. I will spray pesticide **2 times**—herbicide once before emergence, and insecticide once when the corn borer appears. I expect about **500 kg per mu** of maize.

I do not try new crops or fancy methods. At my age, I do not have the energy or the money to take risks. Wheat and maize give me grain to eat, straw to feed my animals, and a little cash from what I sell. That is enough.
